## TRA Timeline

#### Up-C IPO and TRA execution

- 2021-10-20: Form-of TRA filed as Exhibit 10.1 to S-1/A Amendment No. 1 with blank preamble date
- 2021-10-27: Up-C IPO closes; TRA executed at 85% sharing rate with Solo Stove Holdings LLC, the TRA Representatives, and the TRA Parties
- 2021-12-09: Executed TRA filed as Exhibit 10.1 to Q3 2021 10-Q (no Item 1.01 8-K was filed at IPO)

#### Up-C collapse without TRA termination

- 2025-12-17: Merger agreement signed to collapse the Up-C structure; 8-K explicitly confirms the TRA will not be terminated, accelerated, or modified
- 2026-01-01: Up-C collapse merger effective; TRA remains in force per FY2025 10-K and Q1 2026 10-Q

## Explanation

Solo Brands, Inc. executed a Tax Receivable Agreement on October 27, 2021 at its Up-C IPO close, paying 85% of realized tax benefits to Continuing LLC Owners of Solo Stove Holdings for Section 754 basis step-ups and related attributes. The contract has carried no cash flow across its life: every annual disclosure from FY2021 through FY2025 reports zero payments due and zero paid, reflecting negligible redemption volume by Continuing LLC Owners and a carryforward valuation-allowance posture. In December 2025, Solo Brands collapsed its Up-C structure via merger effective January 1, 2026, but explicitly preserved the TRA rather than terminating it; the 8-K states the merger "will not terminate, or otherwise accelerate or modify, the obligations of the Company under the Tax Receivable Agreement". This is an unusual choice: most Up-C collapses pair with a negotiated termination payment amendment, while Solo Brands chose to retain the contract and rely on the post-collapse tax structure to keep future payment obligations small. See `contract_log.md` for the executed text and the Up-C collapse merger agreement.
